summary.text: A 21-year-old unmarried nulligravida had a one-year history of mild intermittent left iliac fossa pain that worsened over the last three months and four years of intermittent foul-smelling vaginal discharge. Menarche was at 14, cycles were normal, and general physical and abdominal examinations were normal.

Ultrasound of the pelvis prompted consideration of a Robert’s uterus and MRI was advised. MRI showed a well-circumscribed left uterine wall mass with a hemorrhagic cystic cavity lined by endometrium without communication with the main cavity, with normal ovaries, tubes and normal left tubal insertion, and ACUM was confirmed.

She was prescribed oral contraceptive pills and showed a positive response after six months, but experienced the onset of dysmenorrhea in the absence of the medication. Surgical treatment was refused, and medical therapy was described as giving only temporary relief.

summary.text: A 20-year-old unmarried nulligravida presented with mild chronic pelvic pain and severe dysmenorrhea, with menarche at 13 and no history of vaginal discharge. Analgesics were initially ineffective, and she was then shifted to oral contraceptive pills for the past year with partial symptom relief.

Ultrasound showed a well-defined mass embedded in the myometrium near the left cornu with peripheral vascular flow, a central fluid-filled cavity and an echogenic endometrial-type lining, and ACUM was proposed. MRI of the pelvis was then performed to confirm the diagnosis and exclude other uterine pathologies.

She continued oral contraceptive pills, although the response had not been entirely satisfactory. She expressed a desire to avoid surgical intervention, and medical therapy was described as giving only temporary relief.

summary.text: A 32-year-old married woman presented with recurrent left lower abdominal pain for the past three years and had no past history of surgery. She had been investigated for a similar complaint and misdiagnosed twice on ultrasound in a remote area, first with a heterotopic pregnancy and then a chronic left cornual ectopic pregnancy.

Urine analysis for pregnancy was negative. Ultrasound and MRI at the authors' institution diagnosed ACUM, with a mass in the left lateral uterine wall, peripheral vascular flow and hyperintense T1 and T2 signal consistent with hemorrhagic contents.

Because of her desire to conceive a second child she chose analgesics to alleviate her pain instead of hormonal therapy, and she refused surgical treatment. After a six-month follow-up she had symptomatic improvement, but conception had not yet occurred.
